title: Seriously?  Amazon needs to do some vetting of vendors
text:
Seriously? Amazon needs to do some vetting of vendors. I realize the price was cheap, but what came in the tiny box was ridiculous. 120 pieces of paper thin metal tubes, plastic connectors and flimsy "shelving" material (they warn you not to touch your finger to the ends of the tubes, and that's because they're razor thin).
I wanted to return them (I bought 2), and have been offered by the seller, a 10% refund, which I should be happy to take because of the hassle and expense of returning them.
Am I the only one who remembers when, if you bought something from Amazon, you could return it, no questions asked, full refund, and no return postage? Oanan is a nightmare. If you buy it, you own it. 10% doesn't even cover the original postage.
And, here are their instructions: 1) As illustrated to remove the bottom of the A and B installation of the first layer then plug into C. 2) As illustrated to install a layer on the basis of the first step. 3) As illustrated each layer superimposed up. That's it! Accompanied by three 1.5" Square useless "illustrations". Then there's a note: "At the bottom of the shoe rack installed at the bottom of the foot, leg with a plastic to protect prevent slippery wear-resisting, very secure." No kidding! Ver batim, that's what it says!!!!
This company shouldn't even be allowed to sell on Amazon if Amazon wants to keep their customer loyalty.
